reason: The young stars' light interacting with a loose cloud seems a direct way to investigate how nearby gas shines.
expectation: The stars may illuminate or ionize the loose gas, making it glow; I don't know the exact result.

alternatives.reason: The dense cloud could also reveal a way gas shines, but I'll try the loose cloud first.

effect: The loose cloud becomes an outflow rather than clearly satisfying the shining-gas goal; it can now interact with the hot bridge.
reaction: I was surprised that the gas was swept away rather than simply made to glow.
reason: The dense cloud is another direct way to investigate how the young stars affect nearby gas.
expectation: The stars may heat or illuminate the dense cloud, though I'm unsure whether it will glow or produce another outflow.

alternatives.reason: The outflow meeting the hot bridge is interesting, but I want to investigate the other nearby cloud first.

effect: The dense cloud becomes shielded pillars, completing the goal about what remains of the cloud.
reaction: The contrast between eroded surfaces and protected interiors is satisfying.
reason: The thin cloud fringe is another nearby gas component to test against the young stars' light.
expectation: The stars may illuminate or ionize the fringe, making it shine, although the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The outflow meeting the hot bridge may also make gas shine, but the fringe seems more directly exposed to the stars.

effect: The thin fringe glows as ionized hydrogen captures electrons, giving one way to make nearby gas shine.
reaction: The explanation of how the glow arises is satisfying.
reason: The outflow meeting the hot bridge may provide a second way to make gas shine.
expectation: The interaction may heat gas enough to glow, though I'm uncertain about the mechanism.

alternatives.reason: The outflow could also affect the dense pillars, but the hot bridge seems a more direct way to investigate glowing gas.

effect: The outflow mixed with the hot bridge rather than clearly producing a second glow, so I still need another way to make gas shine.
reaction: The meeting of gas from two different histories is interesting, though it wasn't what I expected.
reason: The outflow striking dense pillars may create a different luminous interaction.
expectation: The collision might heat gas and make it glow, but it could instead change the pillars without producing light.

alternatives.reason: Gas falling toward the young star might also shine, but the outflow hitting the pillars seems worth trying first.

effect: The outflow carries dense clumps away from the pillars, but hasn't clearly provided a second way for gas to shine.
reaction: The surviving clumps are interesting, though I expected a possible glow.
reason: I'll try gas falling toward the young star as a possible source of luminous accretion.
expectation: Falling gas may heat up and shine, though I'm unsure how this particular interaction works.

alternatives.reason: Dusty gas falling into the disk may also produce light, but I'll try the more general infalling gas first.

effect: The infalling gas produced a magnetically guided jet rather than an immediate glow; the jet can now interact with the hot bridge.
reaction: The contrast between inward feeding and outward launch was surprising.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the jet striking gas may provide the second way to make it shine.
expectation: The jet may shock and heat the bridge gas, making it glow, though the result is uncertain.

effect: The jet's shock heats gas and makes it glow, providing the second mechanism and completing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the jet lead to a different kind of glow from the ionized fringe.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing the ionized fringe with the jet's shock was most worthwhile: the two interactions made the distinction between ways gas can shine clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the outflow against the pillars was the least directly rewarding for my immediate goal; it carried clumps away rather than producing the glow I was seeking.

surprise.text: I was surprised that infalling gas could help produce an outward jet, rather than simply staying with the star.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, although I was guessing whether the outflow hitting the pillars would make gas glow.

continue.text: Yes. The distinct gas histories and mechanisms were interesting enough that I would choose to see where they lead.
